hero.subtitle.message: A self-hosted CI server, in the spirit of Jenkins / GitHub Actions

hero.desc.message: Start with a single binary and SQLite. Define workflows in YAML, dispatch jobs to any build machine with pull-based Agents, and get real-time updates on every page — no refresh buttons anywhere. The GitHub Actions experience, on your own hardware.

features.desc.message: From a solo developer's packaging script to continuous integration inside the enterprise network — one tool covers it all

feature.dag.desc.message: Declare dependencies with needs to form a DAG. Jobs run in parallel, failed dependencies skip downstream jobs, and the run page renders a Blue Ocean-style graph.

feature.agent.desc.message: Agents dial out to the Master over a gRPC bidirectional stream: pull-based job claiming, heartbeat leases, auto-reconnect, and orphaned-job requeue — no inbound ports needed on build machines.

feature.realtime.desc.message: Every page holds its own SignalR connection and updates live. A heartbeat watchdog retries with exponential backoff — the whole app has no manual refresh button.

feature.log.desc.message: Per-line timestamps, JSONL resume cursors, full ANSI color, per-step log downloads, and timeout kills of the entire process tree.

feature.config.desc.message: Each job's YAML config is its own Git repository: saving in the web editor commits automatically, giving you history, rollback, and git clone for free.

feature.trigger.desc.message: Manual runs with parameters, Git push webhooks (HMAC verification + branch globs), PR/MR triggers, and cron schedules — with commit status written back to GitHub/GitLab.

feature.notify.desc.message: WeCom, DingTalk, Slack, generic webhooks, and SMTP email — filterable per channel, with color-coded success/failure cards.

feature.auth.desc.message: Three-tier RBAC, per-project visibility, personal API tokens, and LDAP domain login with group mapping.

quickstart.desc.message: No database to install, no plugin ecosystem to babysit — two commands and you're live

unity.desc.message: Not a single line of Unity-specific code inside the CI — build knowledge lives in your game repo, the engine only orchestrates

unity.step1.message: Agent self-check: prints build environment variables to confirm UNITY_PATH and working directory

unity.step2.message: Launches the Unity 6 command line (-batchmode -executeMethod), streaming logs to the web terminal line by line

unity.step3.message: Archives artifacts, pushes a WeCom notification, and writes build status back to the commit

unity.note.message: The project stays where it is — CI comes to it: bind a task directly to a local Unity project directory, no need to push gigabytes into Git. From first script to a Windows build: one hour, measured.

cta.title.message: Hand your packaging to Infinity CI

cta.desc.message: Deploy as a single EXE or in Docker. SQLite single-file storage — backing up is copying one directory
